title: Cifral — Scope-of-Supply catalog
description: The canonical, versioned list of scope-of-supply items a proposal can contain. Scope is decided PER REQUEST (not per client): the same reseller may send a full-scope modernization RFQ today and a materials-and-engineering-only RFQ tomorrow. Module 1 extracts a `scope_of_supply` map (item key -> boolean) against these keys; that one map then drives pricing lines (Module 3), which agents run and what they write (Module 2), and which template blocks survive (Module 4). To add or rename a scope item, edit THIS file, then update the extraction hints in Module 1 and the block list in docs/TEMPLATE-GUIDE.md.

changelog.2: Chapter-catalog rework. `narrative_section` (one string) became `sections` (an array of schemas/chapter-catalog.json ids) and `template_block` was dropped — the flag is now derivable as 'has_' + each section id. The old one-narrative-section-per-scope-item mapping FUSED deliverables with execution: `materials`+`engineering` both collapsed into `alcance_tecnico`, and `installation`+`commissioning`+`project_management` all collapsed into `plan_implantacion`. That fusion is why a reader could not tell what is delivered from how it is executed. Splitting it is the point of the rework.
changelog.1: Initial catalog: one narrative section per scope item.

items.description: Physical goods / equipment supplied. Priced via materials_cost (not an hourly category).
On-site assembly/installation labour. Often excluded when the end customer installs themselves.
PM / coordination hours. Note the schedule (gestion_proyecto_planificacion) is NOT gated on this — the client always needs to know when things land, even when they manage the project themselves.
Recommended spare-parts package. Its cost, if any, is folded into materials_cost.
Transport to site. Cost, if any, folded into materials_cost.
Warranty clause. Boilerplate-only; no direct cost line.
